profile.campus: Henderson, Clark County, Nevada (West Warm Springs Road, 64-acre site, two parcels east of Boulder Highway)
profile.address: 560 West Warm Springs Road, Sierra Vista City, Henderson, Clark County, Nevada, 89011
profile.reading:
This building, addressed 560 West Warm Springs Road, is the second of two Google has built on a 64-acre Henderson, Nevada site spanning two parcels east of Boulder Highway. Google subsidiary Design LLC filed the original application through Nevada's Governor's Office of Economic Development, and Clark County approved it in November 2018 as a $600 million project expected to create at least 50 permanent positions averaging around $31 an hour, plus more than 3,000 temporary construction jobs. Henderson Mayor Debra March and Google formally announced the partnership in July 2019, and the state granted Google roughly $25 million in tax abatements over 20 years while the company was still projected to pay more than $85 million in state and local taxes over that period. Google returned to expand the project less than two years later: in September 2020 the company announced an additional $600 million investment, doubling its cumulative Henderson commitment to $1.2 billion and adding at least 50 more full-time positions at an average annual salary of about $65,000. The facility supports Google Cloud alongside core consumer services including Search, YouTube, and Gmail for the western United States. Google's Nevada data center location page did not resolve to a working page when checked this session, so this reading relies on Las Vegas Sun and Las Vegas Review-Journal reporting rather than Google's own site; Google has not disclosed which of the two Warm Springs Road buildings, 540 or 560, serves which function, nor either building's individual square footage or MW capacity.

NV Energy, the regulated utility serving Henderson, has cited large-load data center customers including Google among the drivers behind its own long-range resource planning filings with the Nevada Public Utilities Commission, and Nevada's state and local incentive packages for data centers, including the abatements Google received, have periodically drawn scrutiny from state lawmakers weighing how much tax revenue such deals forgo against the jobs and investment they attract.

reading.body:
Google operates a data center campus in Henderson, Nevada, confirmed on the company's own location pages. The facility's exact power capacity is not published. Google's disclosure policy does not include megawatt figures for individual buildings, only aggregate investment numbers at state level.

Nevada has 26 mapped data center facilities, of which only two publish power specifications. This Henderson campus ranks third among Nevada's published capacity, though the state total of published capacity across all operators is 10.37 MW, a figure that reflects disclosure gaps rather than actual deployment. Without published specifications, this facility cannot be evaluated against the compute density and scaling trajectory that drive AI capability.

The location is confirmed but opaque. The absence of published capacity means this site cannot be read as evidence of Google's AI infrastructure plans in Nevada or contribution to regional grid constraint. Evaluating whether this campus matters to AI scaling requires data Google has not released.
